subject: chemistry
instructions: Section A is compulsory. Attempt any four questions from Section B. The intended marks for questions or parts of questions are given in brackets [].

sections.name: Section B
sections.rule: Attempt any four questions from this Section

questions.question: An element in period 3, whose electron affinity is zero:
questions.solution: (d) Argon. It is a noble gas of period 3 whose electron affinity is zero.

questions.question: An element with the largest atomic radius among the following is:
questions.solution: (c) Lithium. Atomic radii decrease across a period from left to right.

concepts: ores of aluminium vs electrolyte additives
questions.question: The compound that is not an ore of aluminium:
questions.solution: (c) Fluorspar (CaF2). The others are ores/minerals of aluminium. (Printed key: option c.)

questions.question: The vapour density of CH3OH is .............. . (At. Wt. C=12, H=1, O=16)
questions.solution: (c) 16. Molecular mass of CH3OH = 12 + 3 + 16 + 1 = 32; vapour density = 32/2 = 16.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions takes place at the anode during the electroplating of an article with silver?
questions.solution: (a) Ag - 1e- -> Ag1+. Oxidation takes place at the anode.

concepts: Cu2+ with excess NH4OH inky blue
questions.question: The metallic hydroxide which forms a deep inky blue solution with excess ammonium hydroxide solution is:
questions.solution: (b) Cu(OH)2. Cu2+ ions form a deep inky blue solution with excess NH4OH.

questions.question: An example of a cyclic organic compound is:
questions.solution: (d) Benzene. It has all carbon atoms in a ring structure.

questions.question: In the laboratory preparation, HCl gas is dried by passing through:
questions.solution: (b) concentrated sulphuric acid. Other drying agents react with HCl gas.

concepts: thermal decomposition of nitrates; PbO colour
questions.question: The nitrate which on thermal decomposition leaves behind a residue which is yellow when hot and white when cold:
questions.solution: (d) Zinc nitrate: on heating it leaves zinc oxide, which is yellow when hot and white when cold. (The printed key shows (a) lead nitrate, but lead oxide is reddish-brown when hot and yellow when cold.)

concepts: conc. H2SO4 with nitrate: KHSO4 vs K2SO4 at high temperature
questions.question: The salt formed when concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with KNO3 above 200 deg C:
questions.solution: (a) K2SO4. Above 200 deg C, KNO3 reacts with concentrated H2SO4 to form the normal salt: 2KNO3 + H2SO4 -> K2SO4 + 2HNO3. (Below 200 deg C the acid salt KHSO4 forms; the printed solution shows (c) KHSO4, which does not fit the 'above 200 deg C' condition.)

questions.question: The property exhibited by concentrated sulphuric acid when it is used to prepare hydrogen chloride gas from potassium chloride:
questions.solution: (d) Non-volatile acid property.

questions.question: The hydrocarbon formed when sodium propanoate and soda lime are heated together:
questions.solution: (b) Ethane (decarboxylation: C2H5COONa + NaOH -> C2H6 + Na2CO3).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
concepts: acid salts and basicity of acids
questions.question: The acid which does not form acid salt by a basic radical:
questions.solution: (d) CH3COOH: acetic acid is monobasic, so it cannot form an acid salt. (The printed key shows (a) H2CO3, but carbonic acid is dibasic and does form acid salts such as bicarbonates.)

questions.question: The general formula of hydrocarbons with single covalent bonds is:
questions.solution: (a) CnH2n+2 (alkanes).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: The indicator which changes to pink colour in an alkaline solution is:
questions.solution: (d) Phenolphthalein.

concepts: properties of ionic vs covalent compounds
questions.question:
Match the Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Sodium Chloride (b) Methane (c) Hydrogen chloride gas (d) Oxidation reaction (e) Water
Column B: 1. has two shared pair of electrons 2. has high melting and boiling points 3. a greenhouse gas 4. has low melting and boiling points 5. Zn - 2e- -> Zn2+ 6. S + 2e- -> S2-

accepted: has high melting and boiling points
has low melting and boiling points
has two shared pair of electrons
has two shared pair of electrons
has low melting and boiling points

questions.solution: (a) Sodium chloride - 2 (high melting and boiling points). (b) Methane - 3 (a greenhouse gas). (c) and (e): water has TWO shared pairs of electrons (two O-H bonds) so Water - 1; hydrogen chloride has ONE shared pair and is a covalent gas with low melting and boiling points, so HCl - 4. (The printed key pairs them the other way round; both pairings are accepted here.) (d) Oxidation reaction - 5 (Zn - 2e- -> Zn2+).

questions.question:
The following sketch illustrates the process of conversion of Alumina to Aluminium. Study the diagram and answer the following:
(a) Name the constituent of the electrolyte mixture which has a divalent metal in it.
(b) Name the powdered substance 'X' sprinkled on the surface of the electrolyte mixture.
(c) What is the name of the process?
(d) Write the reactions taking place at the electrodes 'Y' (anode) and 'Z' (cathode) respectively.
questions.solution: (a) Fluorspar (CaF2); the electrolyte is fused alumina + cryolite + fluorspar, and calcium is the divalent metal. (b) Powdered coke, sprinkled to reduce heat loss by radiation. (c) Hall-Heroult process. (d) At anode (Y): 6O2- -> 3O2 + 12e-. At cathode (Z): 2Al3+ + 6e- -> 2Al.
questions.figure_desc: Sketch of the electrolytic cell for extraction of aluminium: a steel tank lined with carbon (cathode) containing fused alumina, cryolite and fluorspar, with carbon anode rods labelled Y, cathode labelled Z, and a powdered substance X sprinkled on the surface of the electrolyte.

questions.question:
State the terms/process for the following:
(a) The energy released when an atom in the gaseous state accepts an electron to form an anion.
(b) Tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms.
(c) The name of the process by which Ammonia is manufactured on a large scale.
(d) A type of salt formed by partial replacement of hydroxyl radicals with an acid radical.
(e) The ratio of the mass of a certain volume of gas to the same volume of hydrogen measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.

answer_items.prompt: Energy released when a gaseous atom accepts an electron to form an anion
Tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms
Process of large scale manufacture of ammonia
Salt formed by partial replacement of hydroxyl radicals with an acid radical
Ratio of mass of a volume of gas to the same volume of hydrogen

questions.solution: (a) Electron affinity; (b) Catenation; (c) Haber's process; (d) Basic salt; (e) Vapour density.

questions.question:
(a) Draw the structural formula of the following organic compounds:
1. 2-chlorobutane
2. Methanal
3. But-2-yne
(b) Give the IUPAC name of the following organic compounds (structures given in the paper):
1. [structure of CH3COOH]
2. [structure of a four-carbon alcohol with OH on carbon 2]
questions.solution: (a) 1. 2-chlorobutane: CH3-CHCl-CH2-CH3. 2. Methanal: H-CHO (H2C=O). 3. But-2-yne: CH3-C≡C-CH3. (b) 1. Ethanoic acid (acetic acid). 2. Butan-2-ol.
questions.figure_desc: Part (b) shows two structural formulae to be named; the printed answer indicates 1 is the carboxylic acid CH3COOH (acetic/ethanoic acid) and 2 is butan-2-ol (CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3). Structures themselves are not reproduced in the text.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Arrange the following as per the instruction given in the brackets:
(a) Al, K, Mg, Ca (decreasing order of its reactivity)
(b) N, Be, O, C (increasing order of non-metallic character)
(c) P, Si, F, Be (decreasing order of valence electrons)
questions.solution: (a) K > Ca > Mg > Al (correct reactivity series). PRINTED KEY gives K > Al > Ca > Mg, which is wrong; accept either. (b) Be < C < N < O (non-metallic character increases across the period). (c) F > P > Si > Be (7, 5, 4, 2 valence electrons).

marking_points.point: (a) K > Ca > Mg > Al (printed key K > Al > Ca > Mg also accepted)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Complete and balance the following equations:
(a) NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 ->
(b) CuSO4 + NH4OH ->
(c) Cu + Conc. HNO3 ->
questions.solution: (a) 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2NH3 + 2H2O. (b) CuSO4(aq) + 2NH4OH(aq) -> Cu(OH)2(s) + (NH4)2SO4(aq). (c) Cu + 4HNO3 -> Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O (the 3Cu + 8HNO3 -> 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O version is also accepted as printed).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
State a relevant reason for the following:
(a) Hydrogen chloride gas cannot be dried over quick lime.
(b) Ammonia gas is not collected over water.
questions.solution: (a) HCl is acidic and quicklime (CaO) is basic, so they react: 2HCl + CaO -> CaCl2 + H2O. (b) Ammonia is highly soluble in water, so it cannot be collected over water; it is collected by downward displacement of air.

marking_points.point: (a) HCl is acidic and CaO is basic, so they react (2HCl + CaO -> CaCl2 + H2O)
(b) Ammonia is highly soluble in water

(a) aluminium, magnesium, manganese, copper
(b) iron, nickel, chromium, carbon
questions.solution: (a) Duralumin; (b) Stainless steel.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Solve the following numerical problem.
Ethane burns in oxygen according to the chemical equation:
2C2H6 + 7O2 -> 4CO2 + 6H2O
If 80 ml of ethane is burnt in 300 ml of oxygen, find the composition of the resultant gaseous mixture when measured at room temperature.
questions.solution: By Gay-Lussac's law, C2H6 : CO2 = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2, so 80 ml ethane gives 2 x 80 = 160 ml CO2. O2 : C2H6 = 7 : 2 = 3.5 : 1, so O2 needed = 3.5 x 80 = 280 ml. Remaining O2 = 300 - 280 = 20 ml. Water is liquid at room temperature. The resultant gaseous mixture is 160 ml CO2 and 20 ml O2.

marking_points.point: Oxygen used = 280 ml, unused oxygen = 300 - 280 = 20 ml
Composition: 160 ml CO2 and 20 ml O2 (water is liquid)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The following questions are pertaining to the laboratory preparation of Ammonia gas from Magnesium nitride:
(a) Write a balanced chemical equation for its preparation.
(b) Why is this method seldom used?
(c) How do you identify the gas formed?
questions.solution: (a) Mg3N2 + 6H2O -> 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3. (b) Magnesium nitride is very expensive. (c) Bring a glass rod dipped in conc. HCl near the gas; dense white fumes of ammonium chloride are formed.

marking_points.point: (b) It is a very expensive method
(c) Dense white fumes with a rod dipped in HCl

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Electron dot structures NH4+ and N2
questions.question:
Draw the electron dot structure for the following:
(a) Ammonium ion
(b) A molecule of nitrogen
[At. No.: N = 7, H = 1]
questions.solution: (a) NH4+: nitrogen is at the centre with four shared pairs, one to each of four hydrogen atoms; three N-H bonds are formed by sharing and the fourth by a coordinate bond (a lone pair of N donated to H+); the whole is enclosed in brackets with a + charge. (b) N2: each N has 5 valence electrons; three pairs of electrons are shared between the two atoms (N:::N, triple bond) and each N keeps one lone pair.

marking_points.point: (a) Correct NH4+ structure: N with four shared pairs to H, one a coordinate bond, in brackets with + charge
(b) N2 with three shared pairs and one lone pair on each N

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give a balanced chemical equation for the following conversions with conditions:
(a) Ethene from ethanol
(b) Ethyne from calcium carbide
(c) Monochloromethane from methane
questions.solution: (a) C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O (conc. H2SO4, 170 deg C). (b) CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. (c) CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl (diffused sunlight / UV light).

marking_points.point: (a) C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O with conc. H2SO4 at 170 deg C
(c) CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl in sunlight/UV

concepts: anion tests: nitrate brown ring/Cu test
questions.question:
Study the following observations and name the anions present in each of the reactions.
(a) When a crystalline solid 'P' is warmed with concentrated H2SO4 and copper turnings a reddish brown gas is released.
(b) When few drops of dilute sulphuric acid is added to Salt 'R' and heated, a colourless gas is released which turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black.
(c) When few drops of barium nitrate solution is added to the salt solution 'Q', a white precipitate is formed which is insoluble in HCl.
questions.solution: (a) Nitrate (NO3-); reddish brown gas is NO2. (b) Sulphide (S2-); the gas is H2S. (c) Sulphate (SO4 2-).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Define/State:
(a) Electronegativity
(b) Gay-Lussac's Law of combining volumes
questions.solution: (a) Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself. (b) Gay-Lussac's law: when gases react, they do so in volumes which bear a simple whole number ratio to one another and to the volumes of the gaseous products, all volumes being measured under similar conditions of temperature and pressure.

marking_points.point: (a) Tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons
(b) Gases react in volumes in a simple whole number ratio to each other and to gaseous products at the same temperature and pressure

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: The Empirical formula of an organic compound is CHCl2. If its relative molecular mass is 168, what is its molecular formula? [At. Wt. C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5]
questions.solution: Empirical formula mass of CHCl2 = 12 + 1 + 2 x 35.5 = 84. n = 168/84 = 2. Molecular formula = (CHCl2)2 = C2H2Cl4.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Choose the substances given in the box below to answer the following questions:
Box: Iron, Magnesium sulphite, Zinc, Sodium sulphide, Lead, Ferric chloride, Copper, Ferrous sulphate
(a) The metal that will not produce hydrogen gas when reacted with dilute acids.
(b) The compound that will produce sulphur dioxide gas when reacted with dilute HCl.
(c) The solution of this compound produces dirty green precipitate with NaOH.
questions.solution: (a) Copper (does not react with dilute acids). (b) Magnesium sulphite: MgSO3 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2O + SO2. (c) Ferrous sulphate (Fe2+ gives a dirty green precipitate of Fe(OH)2 with NaOH); the printed key names it 'ferrous sulphite', a slip for ferrous sulphate.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Observations in ammonia and hydroxide reactions
questions.question:
State one relevant observation for each of the following:
(a) To the copper nitrate solution, initially few drops of sodium hydroxide solution is added and then added in excess.
(b) Burning of ammonia in excess of oxygen.
(c) Dry ammonia gas is passed over heated PbO.
questions.solution: (a) A light blue precipitate of Cu(OH)2 forms initially; it is insoluble in excess NaOH (Cu(NO3)2 + 2NaOH -> Cu(OH)2 + 2NaNO3). (The printed key says the precipitate dissolves in excess giving a deep blue solution; that is true for excess NH4OH, not NaOH; accept either as printed.) (b) Ammonia burns with a yellowish-green flame (forming nitrogen and water). (c) Yellow PbO is reduced to grey/silvery lead (water and nitrogen also formed).

marking_points.point: (a) Light blue precipitate with a few drops of NaOH (excess: precipitate stays / per key dissolves)
(c) PbO is reduced to grey lead

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give reason for the following:
(a) Ionisation potential decreases down a group.
(b) Ionic compounds do not conduct electricity in solid state.
questions.solution: (a) Down a group atomic size increases, so the force of attraction between the nucleus and the valence electron decreases and the electron is easier to remove. (b) In the solid state the ions are held in fixed positions and are not free to move; in the molten state or solution they are free to move and conduct.

marking_points.point: (a) Atomic size increases down the group, so nuclear attraction on the valence electron is less and it is easily removed
(b) In the solid state ions are not free to move

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Calculate:
(a) The percentage of phosphate in the fertilizer super phosphate Ca(H2PO4)2 correct to 1 decimal point. [At. Wt. H = 1, P = 31, O = 16, Ca = 40]
(b) Write the empirical formula of C8H18.
questions.solution: (a) Molar mass of Ca(H2PO4)2 = 40 + 2(2 + 31 + 64) = 234. Mass of P = 2 x 31 = 62. Percentage of phosphorus = 62/234 x 100 = 26.5% (as in the printed key). (b) C : H = 8 : 18 = 4 : 9, so the empirical formula is C4H9.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Answer the following questions with reference to electrorefining of copper:
(a) What is the anode made of?
(b) What do you observe at the cathode?
(c) Write the reaction taking place at the cathode.
questions.solution: (a) A block of impure copper. (b) Reddish-brown copper is deposited at the cathode (Cu2+ ions gain electrons). (c) Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu.

marking_points.point: (b) Reddish-brown copper deposits on the cathode

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Arrange the following according to the instructions given in brackets:
(a) C2H2, C3H6, CH4, C2H4 (In the increasing order of the molecular weight)
(b) Cu2+, Na+, Zn2+, Ag+ (The order of preferential discharge at the cathode)
questions.solution: (a) CH4 (16) < C2H2 (26) < C2H4 (28) < C3H6 (42). (The printed key writes C3H4 = 40 for C3H6; the order is the same.) (b) Ag+ > Cu2+ > Zn2+ > Na+ (ions lower in the electrochemical series are discharged more easily).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: salts of dibasic vs monobasic acids
questions.question:
Differentiate between the following pairs based on the criteria given in the brackets:
(a) Cane sugar and hydrated copper sulphate [using concentrated H2SO4]
(b) Sulphuric acid and hydrochloric acid [type of salts formed]
questions.solution: (a) Cane sugar chars to a black spongy mass of carbon (sugar charcoal); blue hydrated copper sulphate crystals turn to white anhydrous powder (dehydration). (b) Sulphuric acid is dibasic and forms two types of salts, acid salts (bisulphates, e.g. NaHSO4) and normal salts (sulphates); hydrochloric acid is monobasic and forms only one type, chlorides.

marking_points.point: (a) Cane sugar turns black (carbon) while blue CuSO4.5H2O turns white
(b) H2SO4 forms sulphates and bisulphates (two kinds of salts) while HCl forms only chlorides

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Convert the following reactions into a balanced chemical equation:
(a) Ammonia to nitric oxide using oxygen and platinum catalyst.
(b) Sodium hydroxide to sodium sulphate using sulphuric acid.
(c) Ferrous sulphide to hydrogen sulphide using hydrochloric acid.
questions.solution: (a) 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O (Pt catalyst, Ostwald process). (b) H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O. (c) FeS + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2S.
